title: two creators sent me the real prompts behind their games, not a cleaned up recap
author: shaymagen
selftext:
hey, i run vibe1up, a free site that lists AI-made browser games. 932 of them are on there right now. most of the "prompts" we show are just our own starter recipes, but this week two creators actually sent in what they used, and we checked it was them before putting it up.

STAR AGAINST THE DARK by Ant Games is a survivor-like roguelite in the browser, no download or account. you're a star and the worlds orbiting you are your weapons, five epochs and five bosses. they said there wasn't one prompt. a team of claude code agents wrote about 43,000 lines over a lot of sessions, working from one written brief. the standing orders were basically: make it fair and never pay to win, do all the music and sound in code, and keep it as one page that still runs offline. the agents even wrote the game's own WebGL2 renderer.

CarveMania by Alec Salisbury is ski racing in the browser, slalom, giant slalom, super-G and downhill, and it works on your phone. alec said it also wasn't a single prompt. he put together a detailed spec and an implementation plan, then built it step by step with claude code (opus 5.5). every run gets replayed on the server so the world records are real, which i thought was a smart way to stop fake times.



if you've shipped a game this way, did you start from a big brief like ant games, or a spec like alec? curious what actually held up once the game got big.
